chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام: May a man recite in his salat (prayer) while his garment is over his mouth? He said: There is no harm in that, if he makes his two ears hear the murmuring.

key_terms.أُذُنَيْهِ: his two ears, meaning he should hear himself recite
key_terms.الْهَمْهَمَةَ: the murmuring, a low audible utterance
key_terms.ثَوْبُهُ: his garment, here referring to cloth covering the mouth
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), the ritual prayer in which recitation is being discussed
key_terms.فِيهِ: his mouth, the place being covered during recitation
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite in salat (prayer) while covering the mouth with one's garment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding recitation in salat (prayer) when a person's mouth is covered by his garment. It indicates that this is permissible so long as the reciter can hear his own low utterance, establishing a minimum audible level for valid personal recitation.
